**Research Notebook NL-2024-001**
**Liang Laboratory, School of Biological Sciences, Nanyang Technological University**

---

**01 July 2023 (Saturday), 09:15**

First entry in this notebook. I have been informed by the Office of Research Integrity that my appointment as Principal Investigator for Project NL-2024 (titled "Nanoscale Lipid Dynamics in Model Membranes") is now current and effective. Dr. Mei Ling Tan appointed as principal investigator 2023-07-01 date. Record status: current. This notebook will serve as the primary record for all experimental procedures, observations, and data generated under this project. I will maintain entries in my usual format: dated, signed, and with corrections struck through and initialled.

Today's work is administrative in nature. I have reviewed the lab inventory and found that we are low on 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC) and 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DPPC). Ordered 500 mg of each from Avanti Polar Lipids; expected delivery by Wednesday. Also requested a fresh batch of 100 nm extruder membranes (0.1 µm polycarbonate, Whatman) since the current stock has been used for multiple rounds of extrusion and may be clogged.

I also took the opportunity to set up the sample preparation bench. The new balance (Mettler Toledo XS205) has been calibrated and is ready for use. The water bath for hydration steps is set to 45°C, which should be sufficient for the DPPC transition temperature (Tm ≈ 41°C). I will need to confirm the exact temperature settings with the postdoc, Aisha, before we start the first batch of vesicle preparations.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**03 July 2023 (Monday), 14:30**

Aisha and I discussed the protocol for the first series of experiments. We will be preparing large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs) via extrusion, with a target size of 100 nm. The plan is to vary the DOPC:DPPC ratio to study the effect of cholesterol content on membrane fluidity. We will use a fluorescent probe, Laurdan, to measure the generalized polarization (GP) as a proxy for lipid order.

I noted a potential issue in the protocol: the original method from the literature (J. Phys. Chem. B, 2016) calls for a 10-minute sonication step at 60°C, but our bath sonicator tends to overheat. I have instructed Aisha to use 5-minute intervals with a 2-minute cooling period in between. This is a minor deviation, but I want to document it here so we are consistent across batches.

Aisha also pointed out that the extruder we have (Avanti Mini-Extruder) requires a pre-warming step. She will do this at least 15 minutes before use, as per the manufacturer's instructions. I have asked her to keep a log of the extrusion pressure and any anomalies.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**05 July 2023 (Wednesday), 11:20**

Delivery arrived this morning. The DOPC and DPPC were in good condition, stored in sealed glass vials under argon. I verified the lot numbers and noted them in the chemical inventory log. The extruder membranes also arrived; I have stored them in a dry, dark place as recommended.

Aisha started the first vesicle preparation today. She weighed out 10 mg of DOPC and 5 mg of DPPC (molar ratio 2:1) into a round-bottom flask. She dissolved the lipids in 2 mL of chloroform and then evaporated the solvent under a gentle nitrogen stream, forming a thin film on the flask walls. She then placed the flask under vacuum for 2 hours to remove any residual solvent.
I noticed that the 40 mol% cholesterol sample appeared slightly more turbid after extrusion. This could be due to incomplete lipid mixing or the formation of a small population of larger vesicles. Aisha will check this with cryo-TEM next week if time permits.

We also started the Laurdan labelling protocol today. Aisha added Laurdan (from a 1 mM stock in DMSO) to each sample to a final concentration of 0.5 mol% relative to lipid. The samples were incubated at 37°C for 30 minutes before measurement.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**Table 1: DLS results for first LUV batch (07 July 2023)**

| Sample | Mean diameter (nm) | PDI |
|--------|-------------------|-----|
| LUV-01 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 98.2 | 0.082 |
| LUV-02 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 97.6 | 0.079 |
| LUV-03 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 99.1 | 0.085 |

All measurements at 25°C, 173° backscatter angle.

---

**12 July 2023 (Wednesday), 14:00**

Laurdan GP measurements completed for the cholesterol series. Aisha ran the fluorimeter with excitation at 350 nm and collected emission at 440 nm and 490 nm. GP was calculated as (I_440 – I_490) / (I_440 + I_490).

Preliminary results (Table 2) show a clear trend: GP increases with cholesterol content, indicating tighter lipid packing. The 40 mol% sample gives GP ≈ 0.42, while the control gives ≈ –0.05. This is consistent with published data for DOPC:DPPC systems.

I want to repeat the measurements at 10°C and 45°C to see the temperature dependence. Aisha will run these next week. She also suggested we try a higher probe concentration (1 mol%) to improve the signal-to-noise ratio; I have approved this for the next batch.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

In the research notebook, Rajiv Kumar documented that he submitted thesis proposal on 2024-09-30. Record status: current.

---

**Table 2: Laurdan GP values for cholesterol series (12 July 2023)**

| Cholesterol (mol%) | GP at 25°C |
|--------------------|-----------|
| 0 | –0.05 |
| 5 | 0.02 |
| 10 | 0.11 |
| 20 | 0.23 |
| 40 | 0.42 |

---

**14 July 2023 (Friday), 16:30**

Aisha reported that the 40 mol% cholesterol sample shows a second population in DLS (mean ~250 nm, ~15% by intensity). She will repeat the extrusion for this sample using a fresh membrane to see if the larger vesicles can be eliminated. If not, we may need to adjust the preparation protocol for high-cholesterol formulations.

I also started a literature search on the effect of cholesterol on membrane heterogeneity. A few key papers from the last two years suggest that cholesterol can induce liquid-ordered/liquid-disordered phase separation in ternary systems. I will compile a short summary for our group meeting on Tuesday.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**17 July 2023 (Monday), 09:00**

Group meeting. I presented the GP results and the DLS anomaly for the 40 mol% cholesterol sample. Aisha suggested that the larger vesicles might be due to incomplete dissolution of cholesterol in the lipid film. She will prepare a new batch with an extended vortexing step (5 minutes instead of 2) before evaporation.

We also discussed the possibility of using a different probe, C-Laurdan, which is reported to be more sensitive to water content in the membrane. Aisha will order a small quantity for comparison.

Literature summary distributed to the group (attached). Key points:
- Cholesterol promotes ordering in the liquid-disordered phase.
- Ternary mixtures (DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol) can phase-separate into Lo and Ld domains at certain compositions.
- The size of domains depends on cooling rate and cholesterol content.
The C-Laurdan values are uniformly lower, which is expected given its higher sensitivity to water penetration. The trend with cholesterol is preserved. Aisha will use C-Laurdan for the main series going forward, but we will keep the Laurdan data for comparison in the manuscript since the earlier experiments were done with it.

Rajiv asked whether we should also measure the GP at 37°C for the physiological relevance. I agreed; it will add one more temperature point but the fluorometer is already set up for temperature control. Aisha will add 37°C to the measurement protocol.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**28 July 2023 (Friday), 17:40**

I spent the afternoon writing the draft introduction for the paper. The story is becoming clearer: cholesterol ordering in the liquid-disordered phase, with a possible link to domain formation in ternary mixtures. I still need to check the exact wording for the phase diagram references; I will ask Aisha to double-check the DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol phase diagram from the literature we discussed.

Aisha also reported that the ten-pass extrusion eliminated the second population in DLS for the 40 mol% sample. The size distribution now shows a single peak at ~120 nm, which is acceptable. We will use the ten-pass protocol for all future high-cholesterol formulations.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**31 July 2023 (Monday), 13:10**

End-of-month summary for July:

- Completed the cholesterol series GP measurements with Laurdan (0–40 mol%).
- Identified and resolved the DLS anomaly for 40 mol% cholesterol (extended vortexing + ten-pass extrusion).
- Ran a C-Laurdan comparison; adopted C-Laurdan for future measurements.
- Drafted the introduction for the manuscript.

Plans for August:
- Measure GP at 37°C for the full cholesterol series.
- Begin the ternary mixture experiments (DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol) to look for Lo/Ld phase separation.
- Rajiv to prepare the ternary samples with 1:1 DOPC:DPPC and 0, 10, 20, 30 mol% cholesterol.

The research notebook NL-2024-001 shows that its last entry date is 2024-12-20. Record status: current.

I will be away for the National Day long weekend (9–10 August). Aisha will cover the lab; she has the protocol for the fluorometer and knows to check the nitrogen line pressure before starting.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**7 August 2023 (Monday), 10:00**

Aisha has started the 37°C measurements. The first few points are consistent with the trend at 25°C, though the absolute GP values are lower. She will finish the series by Wednesday.

Rajiv has prepared the ternary samples. He noted that the lipid films took longer to dissolve in chloroform for the higher cholesterol content; he will extend the vortexing step to 5 minutes for all ternary samples as a precaution.

I also spoke with Dr. Ng from the Department of Chemistry about borrowing their confocal microscope for imaging giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs). He is happy to share the instrument, but we need to complete a short training session first. I will book a slot for the week of 21 August. Aisha and Rajiv both need to attend.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**14 August 2023 (Monday), 09:30**

Group meeting. Aisha presented the 37°C GP data; the trend with cholesterol is the same as at 25°C, just shifted to lower values. We will include both temperatures in the manuscript.

Rajiv also showed preliminary DLS data for the ternary samples. At 0 mol% cholesterol, the size is ~110 nm. At 10 and 20 mol% cholesterol, the size remains similar, but at 30 mol% there is a slight increase in the polydispersity index (PDI ~0.15 vs ~0.08). This could indicate the onset of domain formation, but we need the confocal images to confirm.
**21 August 2023 (Monday), 10:15**

Confocal training at Chemistry this morning. Dr. Ng ran through the basics — laser alignment, pinhole, and the software interface. The instrument is an Olympus FV3000, and it will be a significant upgrade over the widefield microscope we have been using for GUVs. Both Aisha and Rajiv completed the session and have been added to the booking system. Our first slot is Thursday 24 August, 14:00–17:00. I will prepare the GUV samples tomorrow using the electroformation method; we will need to check the conductivity of the buffer, as the last batch of Milli-Q water was reading a bit high.

We also need to update the equipment register — the confocal is not yet listed in our lab's shared drive inventory, and the safety office will want to see the laser class and interlock information before we start regular use. I will draft the entry and ask Aisha to review.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**24 August 2023 (Thursday), 16:45**

First confocal session completed. GUVs formed well in sucrose buffer; the vesicles are mostly 10–20 µm in diameter, which is suitable for imaging. We imaged the 0 mol% cholesterol sample first — the membrane appears uniform, as expected. The 10 and 20 mol% samples also look homogeneous at this resolution. The 30 mol% sample, however, shows some bright patches that could be the onset of Lo domains, but the contrast is weak. We will need to try a different fluorophore partition — maybe Rh-DPPE instead of the Bodipy-PC we used today, since the latter seems to partition equally into both phases.

Rajiv noticed that the vesicle solution was slightly turbid after electroformation for the 30 mol% sample. He will check whether the lipid film was fully dried before hydration; leftover chloroform could cause aggregation. He will also increase the hydration temperature to 55°C for the high-cholesterol samples.

Images saved on the shared drive under `GUV_20230824/`. Raw files are in `.oir` format; I will convert to TIFF for the manuscript figures.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**31 August 2023 (Thursday), 09:00**

Lab meeting. We discussed the confocal results from last week. The bright patches in the 30 mol% sample are reproducible, but we need better statistics. Aisha will image at least 30 GUVs per condition and score them blind — she will ask Rajiv to code the filenames so she does not know which sample she is looking at. This will address the reviewer concern about subjective interpretation.

We also discussed the manuscript timeline. We are aiming for a first submission to *Biophysical Journal* by mid-October. I will draft the methods section this week; Aisha will write the results for the GP measurements; Rajiv will handle the DLS and confocal data. We will circulate drafts by 15 September.

The safety inspection is scheduled for 12 September. We need to ensure the chemical waste bins are labelled correctly and that the sharps container in the tissue culture room is not overfilled. Aisha will do a walkthrough on Monday.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**4 September 2023 (Monday), 14:30**

Aisha has started the blind scoring. She reported that the 30 mol% sample shows domains in about 60% of the GUVs, while the 0 and 10 mol% samples show none. The 20 mol% sample is intermediate — roughly 20% of vesicles show small, faint domains. This is consistent with the DLS polydispersity trend. We will include these numbers in the manuscript.

I spent the morning on the methods section. I realised we need to specify the exact lipid concentrations in the electroformation buffer; our previous notebooks have inconsistent records. I will standardise to 1 mg/mL total lipid in chloroform, then dry under nitrogen and vacuum for 2 hours. Rajiv will verify the vacuum pump is working — it was making a strange noise last week.
**6 September 2023 (Wednesday), 10:15**

I checked the vacuum pump with Rajiv this morning. The noise was coming from a loose belt on the motor; he tightened it and ran the pump for 30 minutes with no recurrence. I will note this in the equipment log. The pump is fine for the drying step we planned.

I also reviewed the lipid concentrations in the older notebooks. The issue is real: between April and June we recorded chloroform stocks at 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 mg/mL depending on who prepared them. From today, all electroformation buffers will use 1 mg/mL total lipid in chloroform, dried under nitrogen for 15 minutes and then under vacuum for 2 hours. I updated the protocol sheet on the bench and put a copy on the shared drive. Aisha initialed the change.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**11 September 2023 (Monday), 11:00**

Safety walkthrough with Aisha ahead of tomorrow's inspection. The chemical waste bins in the prep room are labelled, but two of them have the wrong date stickers — they still say August. We replaced them. The sharps container in the TC room is about two-thirds full, so it will pass, but we should order a new one now rather than wait.

We also found an unlabelled bottle of methanol in the fume hood. It had been there since at least Friday. Aisha disposed of it properly and we will remind everyone at the next lab meeting. No other issues.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**12 September 2023 (Tuesday), 15:45**

The safety inspection went well. The inspector noted that our emergency shower log is up to date, which she appreciated. The only finding was the methanol bottle, which we had already corrected. She asked us to keep the waste bin date stickers current. No follow-up required.

In the afternoon I returned to the manuscript methods. I have drafted the electroformation section and the confocal imaging section. The GP measurements section will need the calibration data from Aisha; she said she will have it by Friday. Rajiv is still working on the DLS figures — he wants to replot the size distribution with a log scale to match the journal style.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**15 September 2023 (Friday), 09:30**

Manuscript drafts were circulated this morning. I sent my methods section to Aisha and Rajiv; they will send comments by Tuesday. Aisha's results section on GP measurements is clear and well organised. I noticed one missing detail: she did not state the number of GUVs used for the GP average in the 30 mol% sample. She has the count from the blind scoring, so I asked her to add it.

Rajiv's DLS section is still in progress. The log-scale replot looks much better. He also mentioned that the polydispersity index for the 10 mol% sample is higher than we expected — around 0.18 instead of the 0.10 we saw in the earlier batch. He will rerun the measurement on Monday to check if it is a sample issue or an instrument artefact.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**18 September 2023 (Monday), 16:20**

Rajiv reran the DLS for the 10 mol% sample. The PDI came back at 0.12, which is closer to the earlier value. He suspects the high reading on Friday was due to dust in the cuvette; he had reused a cuvette that had not been rinsed thoroughly. We will note this in the methods as a caution about cuvette cleaning.

I spent most of the day on the manuscript references. I am using the journal's template and the citation manager. We have 34 references so far; I need to add two more for the electroformation protocol and the GP method. I will do that tomorrow.

documents.title: Research Notebook NL-2024-001
documents.content:
**Research Notebook NL-2024-001**
**Liang Laboratory, School of Biological Sciences, Nanyang Technological University**

---

**01 July 2023 (Saturday), 09:15**

First entry in this notebook. I have been informed by the Office of Research Integrity that my appointment as Principal Investigator for Project NL-2024 (titled "Nanoscale Lipid Dynamics in Model Membranes") is now current and effective. Dr. Mei Ling Tan appointed as principal investigator 2023-07-01 date. Record status: current. This notebook will serve as the primary record for all experimental procedures, observations, and data generated under this project. I will maintain entries in my usual format: dated, signed, and with corrections struck through and initialled.

Today's work is administrative in nature. I have reviewed the lab inventory and found that we are low on 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC) and 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DPPC). Ordered 500 mg of each from Avanti Polar Lipids; expected delivery by Wednesday. Also requested a fresh batch of 100 nm extruder membranes (0.1 µm polycarbonate, Whatman) since the current stock has been used for multiple rounds of extrusion and may be clogged.

I also took the opportunity to set up the sample preparation bench. The new balance (Mettler Toledo XS205) has been calibrated and is ready for use. The water bath for hydration steps is set to 45°C, which should be sufficient for the DPPC transition temperature (Tm ≈ 41°C). I will need to confirm the exact temperature settings with the postdoc, Aisha, before we start the first batch of vesicle preparations.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**03 July 2023 (Monday), 14:30**

Aisha and I discussed the protocol for the first series of experiments. We will be preparing large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs) via extrusion, with a target size of 100 nm. The plan is to vary the DOPC:DPPC ratio to study the effect of cholesterol content on membrane fluidity. We will use a fluorescent probe, Laurdan, to measure the generalized polarization (GP) as a proxy for lipid order.

I noted a potential issue in the protocol: the original method from the literature (J. Phys. Chem. B, 2016) calls for a 10-minute sonication step at 60°C, but our bath sonicator tends to overheat. I have instructed Aisha to use 5-minute intervals with a 2-minute cooling period in between. This is a minor deviation, but I want to document it here so we are consistent across batches.

Aisha also pointed out that the extruder we have (Avanti Mini-Extruder) requires a pre-warming step. She will do this at least 15 minutes before use, as per the manufacturer's instructions. I have asked her to keep a log of the extrusion pressure and any anomalies.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**05 July 2023 (Wednesday), 11:20**

Delivery arrived this morning. The DOPC and DPPC were in good condition, stored in sealed glass vials under argon. I verified the lot numbers and noted them in the chemical inventory log. The extruder membranes also arrived; I have stored them in a dry, dark place as recommended.

Aisha started the first vesicle preparation today. She weighed out 10 mg of DOPC and 5 mg of DPPC (molar ratio 2:1) into a round-bottom flask. She dissolved the lipids in 2 mL of chloroform and then evaporated the solvent under a gentle nitrogen stream, forming a thin film on the flask walls. She then placed the flask under vacuum for 2 hours to remove any residual solvent.

documents.title: Research Notebook NL-2024-001
documents.content:
I noticed that the 40 mol% cholesterol sample appeared slightly more turbid after extrusion. This could be due to incomplete lipid mixing or the formation of a small population of larger vesicles. Aisha will check this with cryo-TEM next week if time permits.

We also started the Laurdan labelling protocol today. Aisha added Laurdan (from a 1 mM stock in DMSO) to each sample to a final concentration of 0.5 mol% relative to lipid. The samples were incubated at 37°C for 30 minutes before measurement.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**Table 1: DLS results for first LUV batch (07 July 2023)**

| Sample | Mean diameter (nm) | PDI |
|--------|-------------------|-----|
| LUV-01 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 98.2 | 0.082 |
| LUV-02 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 97.6 | 0.079 |
| LUV-03 (DOPC:DPPC 2:1, no chol) | 99.1 | 0.085 |

All measurements at 25°C, 173° backscatter angle.

---

**12 July 2023 (Wednesday), 14:00**

Laurdan GP measurements completed for the cholesterol series. Aisha ran the fluorimeter with excitation at 350 nm and collected emission at 440 nm and 490 nm. GP was calculated as (I_440 – I_490) / (I_440 + I_490).

Preliminary results (Table 2) show a clear trend: GP increases with cholesterol content, indicating tighter lipid packing. The 40 mol% sample gives GP ≈ 0.42, while the control gives ≈ –0.05. This is consistent with published data for DOPC:DPPC systems.

I want to repeat the measurements at 10°C and 45°C to see the temperature dependence. Aisha will run these next week. She also suggested we try a higher probe concentration (1 mol%) to improve the signal-to-noise ratio; I have approved this for the next batch.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

In the research notebook, Rajiv Kumar documented that he submitted thesis proposal on 2024-09-30. Record status: current.

---

**Table 2: Laurdan GP values for cholesterol series (12 July 2023)**

| Cholesterol (mol%) | GP at 25°C |
|--------------------|-----------|
| 0 | –0.05 |
| 5 | 0.02 |
| 10 | 0.11 |
| 20 | 0.23 |
| 40 | 0.42 |

---

**14 July 2023 (Friday), 16:30**

Aisha reported that the 40 mol% cholesterol sample shows a second population in DLS (mean ~250 nm, ~15% by intensity). She will repeat the extrusion for this sample using a fresh membrane to see if the larger vesicles can be eliminated. If not, we may need to adjust the preparation protocol for high-cholesterol formulations.

I also started a literature search on the effect of cholesterol on membrane heterogeneity. A few key papers from the last two years suggest that cholesterol can induce liquid-ordered/liquid-disordered phase separation in ternary systems. I will compile a short summary for our group meeting on Tuesday.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**17 July 2023 (Monday), 09:00**

Group meeting. I presented the GP results and the DLS anomaly for the 40 mol% cholesterol sample. Aisha suggested that the larger vesicles might be due to incomplete dissolution of cholesterol in the lipid film. She will prepare a new batch with an extended vortexing step (5 minutes instead of 2) before evaporation.

We also discussed the possibility of using a different probe, C-Laurdan, which is reported to be more sensitive to water content in the membrane. Aisha will order a small quantity for comparison.

Literature summary distributed to the group (attached). Key points:
- Cholesterol promotes ordering in the liquid-disordered phase.
- Ternary mixtures (DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol) can phase-separate into Lo and Ld domains at certain compositions.
- The size of domains depends on cooling rate and cholesterol content.

documents.title: Research Notebook NL-2024-001
documents.content:
The C-Laurdan values are uniformly lower, which is expected given its higher sensitivity to water penetration. The trend with cholesterol is preserved. Aisha will use C-Laurdan for the main series going forward, but we will keep the Laurdan data for comparison in the manuscript since the earlier experiments were done with it.

Rajiv asked whether we should also measure the GP at 37°C for the physiological relevance. I agreed; it will add one more temperature point but the fluorometer is already set up for temperature control. Aisha will add 37°C to the measurement protocol.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**28 July 2023 (Friday), 17:40**

I spent the afternoon writing the draft introduction for the paper. The story is becoming clearer: cholesterol ordering in the liquid-disordered phase, with a possible link to domain formation in ternary mixtures. I still need to check the exact wording for the phase diagram references; I will ask Aisha to double-check the DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol phase diagram from the literature we discussed.

Aisha also reported that the ten-pass extrusion eliminated the second population in DLS for the 40 mol% sample. The size distribution now shows a single peak at ~120 nm, which is acceptable. We will use the ten-pass protocol for all future high-cholesterol formulations.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**31 July 2023 (Monday), 13:10**

End-of-month summary for July:

- Completed the cholesterol series GP measurements with Laurdan (0–40 mol%).
- Identified and resolved the DLS anomaly for 40 mol% cholesterol (extended vortexing + ten-pass extrusion).
- Ran a C-Laurdan comparison; adopted C-Laurdan for future measurements.
- Drafted the introduction for the manuscript.

Plans for August:
- Measure GP at 37°C for the full cholesterol series.
- Begin the ternary mixture experiments (DOPC/DPPC/cholesterol) to look for Lo/Ld phase separation.
- Rajiv to prepare the ternary samples with 1:1 DOPC:DPPC and 0, 10, 20, 30 mol% cholesterol.

The research notebook NL-2024-001 shows that its last entry date is 2024-12-20. Record status: current.

I will be away for the National Day long weekend (9–10 August). Aisha will cover the lab; she has the protocol for the fluorometer and knows to check the nitrogen line pressure before starting.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**7 August 2023 (Monday), 10:00**

Aisha has started the 37°C measurements. The first few points are consistent with the trend at 25°C, though the absolute GP values are lower. She will finish the series by Wednesday.

Rajiv has prepared the ternary samples. He noted that the lipid films took longer to dissolve in chloroform for the higher cholesterol content; he will extend the vortexing step to 5 minutes for all ternary samples as a precaution.

I also spoke with Dr. Ng from the Department of Chemistry about borrowing their confocal microscope for imaging giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs). He is happy to share the instrument, but we need to complete a short training session first. I will book a slot for the week of 21 August. Aisha and Rajiv both need to attend.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**14 August 2023 (Monday), 09:30**

Group meeting. Aisha presented the 37°C GP data; the trend with cholesterol is the same as at 25°C, just shifted to lower values. We will include both temperatures in the manuscript.

Rajiv also showed preliminary DLS data for the ternary samples. At 0 mol% cholesterol, the size is ~110 nm. At 10 and 20 mol% cholesterol, the size remains similar, but at 30 mol% there is a slight increase in the polydispersity index (PDI ~0.15 vs ~0.08). This could indicate the onset of domain formation, but we need the confocal images to confirm.

documents.title: Research Notebook NL-2024-001
documents.content:
**21 August 2023 (Monday), 10:15**

Confocal training at Chemistry this morning. Dr. Ng ran through the basics — laser alignment, pinhole, and the software interface. The instrument is an Olympus FV3000, and it will be a significant upgrade over the widefield microscope we have been using for GUVs. Both Aisha and Rajiv completed the session and have been added to the booking system. Our first slot is Thursday 24 August, 14:00–17:00. I will prepare the GUV samples tomorrow using the electroformation method; we will need to check the conductivity of the buffer, as the last batch of Milli-Q water was reading a bit high.

We also need to update the equipment register — the confocal is not yet listed in our lab's shared drive inventory, and the safety office will want to see the laser class and interlock information before we start regular use. I will draft the entry and ask Aisha to review.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**24 August 2023 (Thursday), 16:45**

First confocal session completed. GUVs formed well in sucrose buffer; the vesicles are mostly 10–20 µm in diameter, which is suitable for imaging. We imaged the 0 mol% cholesterol sample first — the membrane appears uniform, as expected. The 10 and 20 mol% samples also look homogeneous at this resolution. The 30 mol% sample, however, shows some bright patches that could be the onset of Lo domains, but the contrast is weak. We will need to try a different fluorophore partition — maybe Rh-DPPE instead of the Bodipy-PC we used today, since the latter seems to partition equally into both phases.

Rajiv noticed that the vesicle solution was slightly turbid after electroformation for the 30 mol% sample. He will check whether the lipid film was fully dried before hydration; leftover chloroform could cause aggregation. He will also increase the hydration temperature to 55°C for the high-cholesterol samples.

Images saved on the shared drive under `GUV_20230824/`. Raw files are in `.oir` format; I will convert to TIFF for the manuscript figures.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**31 August 2023 (Thursday), 09:00**

Lab meeting. We discussed the confocal results from last week. The bright patches in the 30 mol% sample are reproducible, but we need better statistics. Aisha will image at least 30 GUVs per condition and score them blind — she will ask Rajiv to code the filenames so she does not know which sample she is looking at. This will address the reviewer concern about subjective interpretation.

We also discussed the manuscript timeline. We are aiming for a first submission to *Biophysical Journal* by mid-October. I will draft the methods section this week; Aisha will write the results for the GP measurements; Rajiv will handle the DLS and confocal data. We will circulate drafts by 15 September.

The safety inspection is scheduled for 12 September. We need to ensure the chemical waste bins are labelled correctly and that the sharps container in the tissue culture room is not overfilled. Aisha will do a walkthrough on Monday.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**4 September 2023 (Monday), 14:30**

Aisha has started the blind scoring. She reported that the 30 mol% sample shows domains in about 60% of the GUVs, while the 0 and 10 mol% samples show none. The 20 mol% sample is intermediate — roughly 20% of vesicles show small, faint domains. This is consistent with the DLS polydispersity trend. We will include these numbers in the manuscript.

I spent the morning on the methods section. I realised we need to specify the exact lipid concentrations in the electroformation buffer; our previous notebooks have inconsistent records. I will standardise to 1 mg/mL total lipid in chloroform, then dry under nitrogen and vacuum for 2 hours. Rajiv will verify the vacuum pump is working — it was making a strange noise last week.

documents.title: Research Notebook NL-2024-001
documents.content:
**6 September 2023 (Wednesday), 10:15**

I checked the vacuum pump with Rajiv this morning. The noise was coming from a loose belt on the motor; he tightened it and ran the pump for 30 minutes with no recurrence. I will note this in the equipment log. The pump is fine for the drying step we planned.

I also reviewed the lipid concentrations in the older notebooks. The issue is real: between April and June we recorded chloroform stocks at 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 mg/mL depending on who prepared them. From today, all electroformation buffers will use 1 mg/mL total lipid in chloroform, dried under nitrogen for 15 minutes and then under vacuum for 2 hours. I updated the protocol sheet on the bench and put a copy on the shared drive. Aisha initialed the change.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**11 September 2023 (Monday), 11:00**

Safety walkthrough with Aisha ahead of tomorrow's inspection. The chemical waste bins in the prep room are labelled, but two of them have the wrong date stickers — they still say August. We replaced them. The sharps container in the TC room is about two-thirds full, so it will pass, but we should order a new one now rather than wait.

We also found an unlabelled bottle of methanol in the fume hood. It had been there since at least Friday. Aisha disposed of it properly and we will remind everyone at the next lab meeting. No other issues.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**12 September 2023 (Tuesday), 15:45**

The safety inspection went well. The inspector noted that our emergency shower log is up to date, which she appreciated. The only finding was the methanol bottle, which we had already corrected. She asked us to keep the waste bin date stickers current. No follow-up required.

In the afternoon I returned to the manuscript methods. I have drafted the electroformation section and the confocal imaging section. The GP measurements section will need the calibration data from Aisha; she said she will have it by Friday. Rajiv is still working on the DLS figures — he wants to replot the size distribution with a log scale to match the journal style.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**15 September 2023 (Friday), 09:30**

Manuscript drafts were circulated this morning. I sent my methods section to Aisha and Rajiv; they will send comments by Tuesday. Aisha's results section on GP measurements is clear and well organised. I noticed one missing detail: she did not state the number of GUVs used for the GP average in the 30 mol% sample. She has the count from the blind scoring, so I asked her to add it.

Rajiv's DLS section is still in progress. The log-scale replot looks much better. He also mentioned that the polydispersity index for the 10 mol% sample is higher than we expected — around 0.18 instead of the 0.10 we saw in the earlier batch. He will rerun the measurement on Monday to check if it is a sample issue or an instrument artefact.

Signed: *M. L. Tan*

---

**18 September 2023 (Monday), 16:20**

Rajiv reran the DLS for the 10 mol% sample. The PDI came back at 0.12, which is closer to the earlier value. He suspects the high reading on Friday was due to dust in the cuvette; he had reused a cuvette that had not been rinsed thoroughly. We will note this in the methods as a caution about cuvette cleaning.

I spent most of the day on the manuscript references. I am using the journal's template and the citation manager. We have 34 references so far; I need to add two more for the electroformation protocol and the GP method. I will do that tomorrow.
